message.content: In lions, the most conspicuous dominant genetic trait is the **normal tawny (golden) coat color**. This phenotype is produced by the wild‑type alleles at several loci that control pigmentation and patterning. The recessive allele that produces the rare white coat (often called “white lions”) is only expressed when an individual inherits two copies of the recessive allele. Thus, the presence of the wild‑type allele at the key pigmentation genes—such as *Taqpep* (which influences the tawny pattern) and *MC1R* (which affects eumelanin production)—results in the dominant tawny coat seen in the vast majority of lions.
